subject.title: [优化建议] 添加结构化错误处理和智能重试机制

question: What cross-platform npm installer failure policy should OpenClaw ship for retries, automatic repair, and fail-closed behavior?
rationale: The request spans first-run UX, platform-specific permission repair, optional setup probes, and security-sensitive npm TLS failures, so automation should not choose retry or remediation semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Conservative diagnostics and transient retries
options.body: Add structured error extraction and remediation text while retrying only clearly transient network failures and leaving certificate/security and persistent local failures explicit.

options.title: Broader automatic repair
options.body: Attempt safe permission or prefix repairs after EACCES-style failures and retry when the repair succeeds, with platform-specific tests and rollback behavior.

options.title: Diagnostics-only first
options.body: Keep install execution behavior mostly unchanged while improving error messages and docs, then revisit retries after specific failures are confirmed.

recommendation.title: Conservative diagnostics and transient retries
recommendation.body: Add structured error extraction and remediation text while retrying only clearly transient network failures and leaving certificate/security and persistent local failures explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest current history on package-manager install targets across POSIX, Windows, and docs touched by this policy.
